# Add Technical Content

Alkahest is designed for technical books, so ordinary source syntax should
remain readable even when a chapter contains code, mathematics, tables,
figures, and citations.

## Code

Use fenced code blocks and name the language for highlighting:

~~~markdown
```python
def half_adder(a: bool, b: bool) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
    return a ^ b, a and b
```
~~~

The result is:

```python
def half_adder(a: bool, b: bool) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
    return a ^ b, a and b
```

Long lines scroll in HTML and wrap safely in print. Builds are static-only:
code is displayed but never executed. Put runnable examples and larger projects
in companion material instead of relying on hidden notebook state.

## Mathematics

Write inline mathematics between dollar signs, such as $E = mc^2$. Put a
displayed equation on its own lines:

$$
V = I R
$$ {#eq-ohms-law}

Refer to it as @eq-ohms-law. Prefer standard Pandoc mathematics that can be
carried consistently into MathML and Typst.

## Tables

Simple pipe tables work across every output:

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `make draft` | Fast HTML writing loop |
| `make check` | Validate author inputs |
| `make build` | Produce routine publication formats |

: Routine build commands {#tbl-routine-commands}

Introduce @tbl-routine-commands in prose. Keep headings short, identify units
in headings, and avoid using empty cells to imply relationships.

## Figures and assets

Put public source images in `assets/` and provide useful alternative text:

```markdown
![A block diagram showing the fetch, decode, and execute stages.](assets/cpu-pipeline.svg){#fig-cpu-pipeline}
```

The path is relative to the book project, even when the reference appears in a
chapter subdirectory. The sentence in brackets is not a caption placeholder;
it must communicate the figure's purpose to someone who cannot see it.

## Callouts, citations, and notes

Use callouts for information that truly needs a distinct role:

```markdown
::: {.callout-warning}
Disconnect power before changing the circuit.
:::
```

Add BibTeX or BibLaTeX records to `references.bib`, cite them with a key such as
`[@quarto-guide]`, and leave `manuscript/references.qmd` as the single generated
bibliography location. The default citation style is Chicago author-date.

Semantic icons, glossary terms, and indexes are available when a book needs
them. Start with ordinary Markdown and add those systems only for a real
editorial need.
